question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The two problems JTB runs into here are the challenge of grounding justification in non-arbitrary basic beliefs without further support, and the risk that entire webs of mutually supporting beliefs could remain isolated from external reality even if internally consistent. These stem directly from restricting ourselves to only belief and knowledge as states, since any attempt to justify a given belief must either terminate without warrant or rely on the very system it's trying to validate.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the truth x justification grid there are four doxastic positions

* JTB = Knowledge
* J FB = justified false belief
* U TB = unjustified true belief
* U FB = unjustified false belief

JTB identifies only the first cell with a distinct epistemic status, and makes Belief the catch-all for everything that is not Knowledge. That is a loss of discriminatory power.

* Justified false belief. A belief can be fully justified and yet false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it fails truth, so with Knowledge/Belief as the only labels it has to be called mere Belief. That lumps a justified, epistemically responsible false belief together with an unjustified, epistemically irresponsible false belief.
* Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true by accident and not justified. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it fails justification, so with the same two labels it again has to be called mere Belief. That lumps a true, albeit lucky, belief together with a false, unjustified belief and obscures the fact that it is true.

In effect Knowledge/Belief with JTB cannot keep justification and truth apart from each other once a belief falls short of Knowledge. Justified false beliefs lose their justification in the classification, and true unjustified beliefs lose their truth in the classification. That is why a finer-grained taxonomy of justified belief / unjustified belief, true belief / false belief is normally introduced.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only the boxes Knowledge and Belief the JTB analysis forces

Knowledge = Justified ∧ True ∧ Belief

Belief = ¬Knowledge

i.e. every combination of Justified / Unjustified and True / False that is not
Justified + True + Belief is thrown into the single residual category Belief.

The four logical positions are therefore

1. JTB = Knowledge
2. JB¬T = Justified False Belief
3. ¬J TB = Unjustified True Belief
4. ¬J ¬T B = Unjustified False Belief

2,3 and 4 are all just Belief.

That gives a coarse grained taxonomy.

* Justification is lost once truth fails. A justified false belief and an
unjustified false belief are both just Belief. There is no epistemic state
in which justification is tracked independently of truth, so a well supported
but false belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a baseless false
belief. In particular the intuitive epistemic value of being justified is
erased for false beliefs.

* Truth is lost once justification fails. A justified false belief and an
unjustified true belief are both just Belief. There is no epistemic state in
which truth is tracked independently of justification, so a lucky,
unjustified true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a well
reasoned mistake. In particular the intuitive distinction between epistemic
luck – an unjustified true belief – and a justified error is erased.

Hence with the binary Knowledge / Belief stock JTB can mark JTB as
Knowledge but it has to lump all three remaining J/T combinations together
as mere Belief, so justification and truth can no longer be assessed apart
from each other. That is the familiar loss of epistemic value/gradience that
is normally stated as the undervaluation of justified false belief and the
overvaluation of unjustified true belief. Gettier aside this is why the JTB
schema needs finer epistemic categories than just Knowledge vs Belief.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On a JTB analysis the logical space of belief is generated by the three
conditions

* B p : you believe p
* T p : p is true
* J p : your belief that p is justified

JTB says

K p  <=>  B p & T p & J p

so in logical space there are four belief-conditions

 J T B  = knowledge
 J ¬T B = justified false belief
 ¬J T B = unjustified true belief
 ¬J ¬T B = unjustified false belief

If you are allowed only the two labels K and B, and you let B be the
complement of K, then every non-knowledge state has to be called a
mere belief. Justification then ceases to be an independent marker
outside of K.

* Justified false belief. J ¬T B is not K because T fails, so on the
two-state taxonomy it is just ‘Belief’. That means a justified false
belief is lumped together with an unjustified false belief. The
epistemic value of justification is lost as soon as truth fails: you
cannot say a justified falsehood is epistemically better than an
unjustified falsehood, and in fact on the two-state reading a
justified belief is thereby committed to be true, otherwise it would
have to be knowledge. So JTB with only K/B cannot accommodate a
justified but false belief as a distinct, positively marked epistemic
condition.

* Unjustified true belief. ¬J T B is not K because J fails, so it is
also just ‘Belief’. The true belief that is true by luck, inference
from a bad reason, etc., is therefore epistemically indistinguishable
from a plain false belief once the label K is removed. Intuitively a
true belief that is produced by sheer luck is epistemically inferior to
a justified true belief, but on a two-state taxonomy the only
difference you can draw is K vs non-K. In effect truth becomes the
only thing that can make a belief rise out of the mere Belief class,
so justification is swallowed up by truth outside of knowledge. That
is the classic JFB / UTB collapse: justified falsehoods cannot be
recorded as justified, and lucky true beliefs cannot be recorded as
true but unwarranted.

That is why the extra states justified belief and warranted false
belief/unwarranted true belief are wanted, and why with only Knowledge
and Belief JTB forces a conflation of justification with truth. Gettier
put aside, these are the two standard non-Gettier misclassification
problems for a bare JTB taxonomy.

1.text:
With JTB knowledge is a species of belief

*K(p) -> B(p) & T(p) & J(p)*

and on the two state taxonomy the only tags you can give a subject about
p are *K* or *B*. Justification is therefore never a state you can be
in, it is only visible through the conjunction of truth and the move
from B to K.

That makes justification parasitic on truth and makes the state *B* a
heterogeneous grab bag.

* Justified false belief is invisible.  If p is false but J(p) holds
the JTB analysis has no state for it.  It is just *B(p)*, and is
indistinguishable on the taxonomy from a plainly unjustified false
belief. Justification as a normative epistemic worth is therefore lost
for the false case: epistemically good falsehoods are lumped with
epistemically bad falsehoods.

* Unjustified true belief is invisible.  If p is true but ~J(p) holds
the JTB analysis has no state for it either. It is just *B(p)*, and is
indistinguishable on the taxonomy from a justified false belief. In
particular you cannot internally mark off a lucky / unjustified true
belief from a warranted true belief. The move B -> K can only be read
off after the fact by the truth of p, so justification is not an
independently trackable epistemic condition.

Hence on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy justification is not an
epistemic state at all. The normative work that JTB wants justification
to do is hidden inside the truth condition, so the taxonomy cannot
represent epistemically good false belief nor epistemically bad true
belief. That is the classic loss of the justified-false and
unjustified-true categories, i.e. the loss of an independent normative
status for justification. Gettier is set aside.
